born '''Enes Kanter'''; May 20, 1992) is a Turkish and American former professional [[basketball]] player who played 11 seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA).{{cite news |last1=Kanter |first1=Enes |date=May 23, 2017 |title=They Can Take Away Your Country, Just Like That |url=https://www.theplayerstribune.com/articles/enes-kanter-turkey-passport |work=[[The Players' Tribune]] |language=en |archive-date=May 14, 2022 |access-date=April 29, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220514045951/https://www.theplayerstribune.com/articles/enes-kanter-turkey-passport |url-status=live }} Born in Switzerland to parents from Turkey, he was raised in Turkey and moved to the United States as a teenager. Freedom was selected as the third overall pick of the [[2011 NBA draft]] by the [[Utah Jazz]], and primarily played the [[Center (basketball)|center]] position. ==Early life and youth career== Enes Kanter Freedom was born on May 20, 1992, in [[Zürich]], Switzerland as Enes Kanter.{{cite news|last1=Allen|first1=Percy|title=Huskies get commitment from 6-foot-10 Turkish star Enes Kanter|url=http://old.seattletimes.com/html/huskies/2010340248_umen24.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171017151212/http://old.seattletimes.com/html/huskies/2010340248_umen24.html|archive-date=2017-10-17 |url-status=dead|work=[[The Seattle Times]]|date=November 23, 2009}} Kanter's parents immigrated to Switzerland from Turkey, and his father also had [[Kurds|Kurdish]] origins.{{Cite web|url=https://www.vox.com/world/2019/11/13/20941804/enes-kanter-nba-turkey-erdogan|title=How NBA player Enes Kanter became a major enemy of Turkey's president|first=Jen|last=Kirby|date=November 13, 2019|website=Vox|access-date=January 25, 2022|archive-date=January 25, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220125140229/https://www.vox.com/world/2019/11/13/20941804/enes-kanter-nba-turkey-erdogan|url-status=live}}{{Cite web|url=https://x.com/EnesFreedom/status/1753443295546458613|title=Enes Kanter FREEDOM (@EnesFreedom) on X|date=February 2, 2024}} His father, Mehmet Kanter, received his [[Doctor of Medicine|M.D.]] from the [[University of Zurich]]. The family then returned to [[Van, Turkey]],{{cite news |first1=Pete |last1=Thamel |author-link=Pete Thamel |title=Turkish Team Says It Paid a Top Kentucky Recruit |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2010/09/08/sports/ncaabasketball/08basketball.html |work=[[The New York Times]] |date=September 7, 2010 |archive-date=December 28, 2016 |access-date=February 24, 2017 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161228033929/http://www.nytimes.com/2010/09/08/sports/ncaabasketball/08basketball.html |url-status=live }} where Kanter grew up. Mehmet Kanter became a professor of [[histology]] and genetics at [[Trakya University]]. Kanter's mother, Gülsüm Kanter, is a nurse.{{Cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1528633/2020/01/13/enes-kanter-charter-school/|title=Enes Kanter fulfills a childhood promise with plan to build his own school|first=Jay|last=King|work=The New York Times|date=January 13, 2020|archive-date=January 25, 2025|access-date=June 13, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20250125022109/https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1528633/2020/01/13/enes-kanter-charter-school/|url-status=live}} Kanter has three younger siblings: two brothers (including basketball player [[Kerem Kanter]]) and one sister.{{cite news|last1=Jobrani|first1=Maz|last2=Von Ghasri|first2=Tehran|last3=Gleason|first3=Kaitlin Eleanor|last4=Kanter|first4=Enes|title=Ep. 20 - NBA Player Enes Kanter|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ppBgdiE4aq0 |archive-url=https://ghostarchive.org/varchive/youtube/20211220/ppBgdiE4aq0 |archive-date=2021-12-20 |url-status=live|work=Back to School with Maz Jobrani|date=August 20, 2019|format=Video interview/podcast}}{{cbignore}} Starting in second grade, Kanter attended [[Hizmet]]-affiliated schools, part of the [[Gülen movement]] in Turkey.{{cite news|last1=Mita|first1=Molly|title=E:60 Goes To Turkey To Tell Enes Kanter's Story|url=https://www.espnfrontrow.com/2019/03/e60-goes-to-turkey-to-tell-enes-kanters-story/|work=[[ESPN]] Front Row|date=March 8, 2019|archive-date=April 8, 2023|access-date=August 21, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230408064742/https://www.espnfrontrow.com/2019/03/e60-goes-to-turkey-to-tell-enes-kanters-story/|url-status=live}} He lived in [[Ankara]] and then moved to [[Istanbul]] to play professional basketball as a teen.{{cite news|first1=Jordan Ritter|last1=Conn|title=Enes Kanter Contains Multitudes|url=https://www.theringer.com/nba/2018/10/11/17962130/enes-kanter-new-york-knicks-turkey|website=[[The Ringer (website)|The Ringer]]|date=October 11, 2018|archive-date=April 1, 2019|access-date=April 1, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190401025014/https://www.theringer.com/nba/2018/10/11/17962130/enes-kanter-new-york-knicks-turkey|url-status=live}} At the age of 17, Kanter moved to the United States to play basketball. He attended [[Findlay Prep]] in [[Henderson, Nevada]], and then [[Mountain State Academy]] in [[Beckley, West Virginia]]; neither school allowed him to play high school basketball because he had already played basketball professionally.{{Cite web|url=https://news.yahoo.com/nba-scouts-keep-eye-kanter-065700343--nba.html|date=24 April 2024|publisher=Yahoo|title=NBA scouts keep eye on Kanter as in [[Simi Valley, California]], where he was able to play basketball for a season. ==Professional career== === Fenerbahçe (2008–2009) === Before moving to the United States, Kanter played under [[Serdar Apaydın]]'s management for the [[Fenerbahçe Men's Basketball|Fenerbahçe]] youth squad between 2006 and 2008{{cite web|title=Enes Kanter hakkında bilgilendirme|url=http://www.fenerbahce.org/detay.asp?ContentID=16528|work=[[Fenerbahçe Basketball]]|language=tr|access-date=February 14, 2015|archive-url=https://archive.today/20150216001942/http://www.fenerbahce.org/detay.asp?ContentID=16528|archive-date=February 16, 2015|url-status=dead}} and then, during the 2008–09 season, Kanter was a seldom-used reserve for the Fenerbahçe senior team.{{cite news|last1=DeCourcy|first1=Mike|title=Enes Kanter a revolutionary case for Kentucky, NCAA|url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/story/2010-04-14/enes-kanter-revolutionary-case-for-kentucky-ncaa|work=[[Sporting News]]|date=April 14, 2010|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100824110049/http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/story/2010-04-14/enes-kanter-revolutionary-case-for-kentucky-ncaa|archive-date=August 24, 2010}} He played in at least nine games with the team: four in the [[EuroLeague]] and five in the [[Turkish Basketball Super League|Turkish Super League]]. Fenerbahçe and the [[Greek Basket League|Greek League]] basketball team [[Olympiacos B.C.|Olympiacos]] both offered Kanter professional contracts, but he declined because he wanted to play high school and college basketball in the United States. In 2009, Kanter moved to the United States, where he enrolled at Stoneridge Preparatory School in [[Simi Valley, California]], and played for the basketball team in 2009–10.{{cite news|last1=O'Neil|first1=Dana|title=Top Euro hoopster to enroll at U.S. high school|url=https://www.espn.com/high-school/story/_/id/4407971/kanter-enroll-findlay-prep/|work=[[ESPN]]|date=August 19, 2009|archive-date=August 21, 2019|access-date=August 21, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190821004201/https://www.espn.com/high-school/story/_/id/4407971/kanter-enroll-findlay-prep/|url-status=live}} At the 2010 [[Nike Hoop Summit]], Kanter played for the international team, recording 34 points and 13 rebounds. His point total was a record for the event, breaking [[Dirk Nowitzki]]'s record set in the 1998 game. Both [[Rivals.com]] and [[Scout.com]] (now known as [[247Sports.com]]) rated Kanter as a five-star prospect, the highest possible rating.{{cite web|title=Enes Kanter|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/player-Enes-Kanter-102889|work=[[Rivals.com]]|via=[[Yahoo Sports]]|access-date=April 21, 2010|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150405111623/https://sports.yahoo.com/ncaa/basketball/recruiting/player-Enes-Kanter-102889|archive-date=April 5, 2015}}{{cite web|title=Enes Kanter Player Profile News|url=https://247sports.com/Player/Enes-Kanter-8009/|work=[[Scout.com]]|via=[[247Sports.com]]|access-date=August 20, 2010|archive-date=May 31, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130531105918/http://247sports.com/Player/Enes-Kanter-8009|url-status=live}} In November 2009 Kanter verbally committed to play for the [[Washington Huskies men's basketball|Washington Huskies]]. Kanter chose Washington over [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]], [[USC Trojans men's basketball|USC]], [[Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball|Indiana]] and [[UNLV Runnin' Rebels men's basketball|UNLV]]. However, he re-opened his recruitment in February 2010, and on April 14, Kanter signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] to play college basketball for [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]].{{cite news|last1=Allen|first1=Percy|title=Oregon prep star dumps Washington for Kentucky|url=http://www2.kusports.com/news/2010/may/20/oregon-prep-star-dumps-washington-kentucky/|work=[[Lawrence Journal-World]]|via=[[Seattle Times]]|date=May 20, 2010|archive-date=July 27, 2018|access-date=February 14, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180727153715/http://www2.kusports.com/news/2010/may/20/oregon-prep-star-dumps-washington-kentucky/|url-status=live}} However, despite signing with the Kentucky Wildcats, the [[NCAA]] declared him permanently ineligible as a collegiate athlete because he received approximately $33,000 from Fenerbahçe in excess benefits. The NCAA ruled that this amount was above and beyond what was considered acceptable.{{cite news|title=Kentucky center Kanter ruled ineligible by NCAA|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/news/story?id=5793192|work=[[ESPN]]|agency=[[Associated Press|AP]]|date=November 12, 2010}}{{cite news|last1=Dawson|first1=Brett|title=Kentucky forward Enes Kanter ruled permanently ineligible|url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/college/mensbasketball/sec/2010-11-11-kentucky-kanter-ineligible_N.htm|work=[[USA Today]]|via=[[The Courier-Journal]]|date=November 12, 2011|archive-date=December 11, 2015|access-date=February 14, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20151211010555/http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/college/mensbasketball/sec/2010-11-11-kentucky-kanter-ineligible_N.htm|url-status=live}}{{cite news |title=NCAA appeal hearing on Kanter scheduled for Thursday |url=http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/feed/2010-09/enes-kanter/story/ncaa-appeal-hearing-on-kanter-scheduled-for-thursday |work=[[Sporting News]]|date=January 7, 2011|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150214224750/http://www.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/feed/2010-09/enes-kanter/story/ncaa-appeal-hearing-on-kanter-scheduled-for-thursday|archive-date=February 14, 2015}} On January 7, 2011, the NCAA denied Kentucky's appeal, upholding that Kanter was permanently ineligible.{{cite news|first1=Pete|last1=Thamel|author-link=Pete Thamel|title=N.C.A.A. Denies Kentucky's Appeal Over Kanter's Eligibility|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2011/01/08/sports/ncaabasketball/08kentucky.html|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=January 7, 2011|archive-date=December 25, 2017|access-date=February 24, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171225093359/http://www.nytimes.com/2011/01/08/sports/ncaabasketball/08kentucky.html|url-status=live}} ===Utah Jazz (2011–2015)=== [[File:Enes Kanter 2011 draft.jpg|thumb|left|upright=0.7|Kanter at the [[2011 NBA draft]]]] Kanter, a center, was drafted third overall by the [[Utah Jazz]] in the [[2011 NBA draft]]. Upon being drafted, he said "I'm so happy, I'm so excited. I know the Utah Jazz fans are crazy and I love them. I will bring the team toughness and post moves, rebounding, everything. I will try to do everything to make the playoffs."{{cite news|first1=Randy|last1=Hollis|title=Utah Jazz select Enes Kanter with third pick|url=https://www.deseret.com/2011/6/24/20199917/utah-jazz-select-enes-kanter-with-third-pick|work=[[Deseret News]]|date=June 23, 2011|archive-date=August 21, 2019|access-date=August 21, 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190821011035/https://www.deseret.com/2011/6/24/20199917/utah-jazz-select-enes-kanter-with-third-pick|url-status=live}} On December 9, 2011, he signed his rookie scale contract with the Jazz following the conclusion of the [[2011 NBA lockout|NBA lockout]].{{cite news|title=Jazz Signs 2011 Lottery Picks |url=https://www.nba.com/jazz/news/jazz_sign_kanter_and_burks.html|work=[[National Basketball Association|NBA]]|date=December 9, 2011}} In 2011–12, he became the 10th Jazz rookie in franchise history to appear in every regular-season game. He also recorded the most rebounds for a Jazz rookie in debut with 11 against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]] on December 27. In the season, he averaged 4.6 points and 4.2 rebounds in 66 games. In 2012–13, Kanter improved his averages in every major statistical category, led the team in scoring three times and rebounding four times, and scored in double-figures 22 times. In 70 games (two starts), he averaged 7.2 points and 4.3 rebounds per game. On March 1, 2013, Kanter had the first 20–20 game of his career with career-highs of 23 points and 22 rebounds to lead the Jazz to a 98–68 victory over the [[Charlotte Bobcats]].{{cite news|title=Bobcats at Jazz, Friday, March 1, 2013 |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20130301/CHAUTA/gameinfo.html|work=[[National Basketball Association|NBA]]|date=March 1, 2013|url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130125031202/http://www.nba.com/games/20130301/CHAUTA/gameinfo.html|archive-date=January 25, 2013}} He later missed the final 10 games of the season due to a dislocated left shoulder. He dominated throughout the tournament, averaging 22.9 points, 16.5 rebounds and 1.5 blocks in 34.6 minutes per game. However, [[Jonas Valančiūnas]] was chosen as the MVP after he averaged 14.3 points, 11.1 rebounds and 2.3 blocks in 23.5 minutes. Kanter went on to earn MVP honors at the [[2009 FIBA Europe Under-18 Championship]] after averaging 18.6 points and 16.4 rebounds while leading Turkey's junior national team to the bronze medal. He declined to play for the senior national team at the [[2010 FIBA World Championship]] which was being held in Turkey as the team went on to win the silver medal.
